obligations: Book normalization ddc log|z|^2 equals a unit Dirac mass; planar Lelong number is the Riesz atom.
Genuine subharmonic weights are locally integrable and their complex Hessians are positive Radon measures.
Atom removal gives a positive distribution and its unique genuine subharmonic representative.
Locally finite Riesz mass and no residual atom permit M<1/t for every prescribed finite t.
Logarithmic potentials of finite disc measures are locally L1 by Fubini.
The fundamental solution and Weyl harmonic-distribution lemma give the local potential/harmonic decomposition.
Jensen for the normalized finite measure is justified by truncated kernels at poles.
The radial exponent 2tM<2 yields uniform translated integrability on the smaller disc.
Harmonic lower bounds and Tonelli give all finite exponential integrabilities of the zero-atom residual.
Unit factors in a holomorphic germ preserve local integrability.
Locally upper-bounded residual gives necessity k+1>a, including divergence at equality.
Holder with b>1 and b(a-k)<1 proves sufficiency.
Allowed integer orders equal floor(a).
Atoms of mass at least one have locally finite support, giving locally principal ideal sheaves.
A finite sum of principal planar ideals has minimum order and the sum map is locally split.
The kernel is a holomorphic bundle of rank r-1; r=1 is immediate.
Partition of unity supplies smooth lifts without global weighted norm conditions.
Differentiating the lift takes values in the kernel bundle.
Pseudoconvex Euclidean domains admit a smooth strictly psh exhaustion; this is the strongly pseudoconvex formulation in CADG I.6.13 and I.7.2.
The unexpanded metric dd rho^2 is positive and dominates the gradient term with factor 2.
Proper exhaustion with bounded gradient gives completeness.
Convex reweighting dominates bundle negative curvature on compact shells while forcing L2 data.
The flat canonical inverse frame preserves curvature; Euclidean domination preserves L2 data under the canonical-valued identification.
The complete-metric vector Bochner inequality on top bidegree gives a positive identity lower bound.
Cutoff/density, Cauchy and Riesz yield the bundle-valued dbar solution.
Distributional holomorphicity in charts gives holomorphic global components.
No global target weighted norms are imposed on these ideal sections.
Planar ideal orders of the target sum are min floor(A+p_i B_i).
When s<1, P/p_i is a probability vector and gives the needed ideal inclusion.
Global lifting makes one-weight remainders admissible for the original sum of global sections.
The already proved one-weight estimate yields (1-s)I, without an attainment assumption.
Finite input norm when s>=1 implies the strict point-order inequality.
Nonmembership would imply sum B_i>=s(k+1-A)>=k+1-A, contradicting integrability.
The zero function and identically zero input are handled explicitly.
Common logarithmic poles with f=1 attain pi and pi/(1-s) for s<1.
Positive finite I with f=z^q excludes a negative universal constant when s>=1.
No n>=2,r>n optimality or closure of the existing full-scope questions is inferred.
